subject: Slate reserved capacity onboarding playbook & rollback triggers
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Martin <jane.martin@slatetherapeutics.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@slatetherapeutics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Slate reserved capacity onboarding playbook & rollback triggers

Jane — attaching the sizing matrix and a proposed cutover playbook to frame the dedicated capacity onboarding for Slate (DEAL-4582). High level ask and proposed cadence below so we can line up procurement and ops windows: 

- Target go-live window: July 16–20 (canary week July 16–18; full swap July 19 w/ 24h monitor).
- Committed throughput: 120k requests/day steady-state, peak bursts ~220k/day (see sizing_matrix.xlsx).
- Preferred GPU family: H100-80GB for model A in mixed precision. Fallback quantized variant will run on A100 if needed.
- Acceptance criteria (pre-swap and post-swap): 95th latency <= 120ms, error rate < 0.5% sustained, token cost within 12% of hosted baseline.
- Canary plan: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% across 4 rolling steps with 60–90m observation windows.
- Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 2% for 10m, 95th latency regression >40% vs baseline, missing KV cache hit-rate target (<60%) during ramp.
- Ops & monitoring: Datadog traces, per-route token/cost breakdown, and a dedicated Slack channel (#slate-onramp).

Ask: can Procurement confirm contract redlines and a DocuSign recipient for the reserved capacity amendment this week? Also please confirm that your infra team can open IP ranges below and grant the VPC peering request before July 10.

Attachments: slate_proposal_v3.pdf, sizing_matrix.xlsx, dag-runbook.txt

Thanks — I’ll schedule a 30m run-through this Thursday to walk the cutover steps if that helps.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

1) Which GPU family do you recommend as the default for cost vs latency (H100 vs A100)? Is the billing different for a reserved commit?
2) During the canary, can we pause traffic or move segments back to hosted instantly if we see regressions? We need to coordinate with our feature-flagging team.

Procurement: can you review the attached amendment and flag any major concerns? We need SLAs and the credit table spelled out.

Jane Martin
Head of AI Platform | Slate Therapeutics
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Martin <jane.martin@slatetherapeutics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jun 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Slate reserved capacity onboarding playbook & rollback triggers

Jane — quick technical notes to help answer Q1/Q2: 

- Recommendation: H100-80GB for model A if you prioritize tail latency and larger context. A100-80GB is still fine if cost sensitivity is higher; expect ~10–18% higher latency vs H100 at 2k token windows for the same batching.
- Billing: reserved capacity pricing is fixed monthly for the committed pool; we show estimated per-token economics in the sizing sheet (column: unit_cost_reserved). If you need a hybrid during the first 30 days we can enable auto-fallback to hosted with a grace buffer to avoid billing surprises.
- Pause/roll-back mechanics: We support immediate traffic routing back to hosted via routing policy. Operationally we recommend a staged rollback (stop new routing + drain on existing replicas) unless you require instant cutover — we can do both but instant cutover may drop in-flight requests.
- Canary ramp specifics:
  * Step 1 (1%): smoke tests, light queries, KV cache warm-up duties.
  * Step 2 (10%): run production prompts + evaluate distributional drift vs hosted baseline.
  * Step 3 (50%): sustained throughput stress test, validate autoscaling thresholds.
  * Step 4 (100%): full switch after 24h monitoring.

I’ve attached a short runbook (dag-runbook.txt) with sequence commands for provisioning jobs, cache priming scripts and the health-check hook URLs. Happy to walk infra through this during the run-through call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jane Martin <jane.martin@slatetherapeutics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Slate reserved capacity onboarding playbook & rollback triggers

Adding ops perspective and a couple of guardrails: 

- Blackout windows: propose no full swap during Monday maintenance windows (0100–0400 local). If you must swap in that window we’ll require a signed exception and a dry-run beforehand.
- Monitoring hooks: we’ll provide a Datadog dashboard template and per-route SLO alerts. Please confirm a Slack webhook or PagerDuty escalation policy to wire into our oncall.
- Rollback procedure:
  1) Move routing off dedicated via policy (instant OR drain mode).
  2) If routing move fails, trigger routing fallback and pause autoscaling.
  3) Open incident, initiate hotfix cadence — expect 30–45m median time-to-fix for common regressions.

Operational approval checklist (we need these before the canary):
- Procurement signature on reserved amendment (DocuSign).
- Network allowlist + VPC peering confirmed.
- Datadog + tracing endpoints active.
- Nightly cache priming scheduled for 48–72h pre-swap.

Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Reliability
Redwood Inference

2) Slate infra: open the VPC peering and add Redwood IP allowlist from the sizing sheet by July 10.
3) Ops: Ben & Karthik will run a 60m dry-run on July 13 at 10:00 PT (requires Slate feature-flagging to enable: stage-traffic routing).
4) Canary week: July 16–18; Full swap target July 19 with 24h observation.

I’ll create the HubSpot milestone and a shared calendar invite for the dry-run + run-through call. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4582

If procurement confirms by Friday we’ll lock the July 13 dry-run — otherwise we’ll push the timeline by one week. Jane, let me know if Slate needs a different blackout preference and I’ll update the runbook.

—Marissa
